We need to produce a JUnit 4 test file ElementTest.java that comprehensively tests all methods in the Element class. Since the class depends on many other classes from jsoup library (Node, Tag, Attributes, Document, etc.), but we can instantiate Element using its constructors, and use its methods that do not require full parsing of HTML (like tagName, attr, etc.). For methods that rely on parsing (Parser.parseFragment, Selector.select, Collector, etc.) we might need to set up simple environment with jsoup library available. However, as we are writing tests for this class as part of jsoup, we can use the library itself; the test will compile with jsoup library. We'll write tests covering: - constructors, tagName, tag, isBlock, id, attr (string and boolean), dataset, parent/parents, child handling: appendChild, prependChild, appendElement, prependElement, child, children, childElementsList (indirect), textNodes, dataNodes, empty, text, ownText, wholeText, hasText, data, className, classNames, hasClass, addClass, removeClass, toggleClass, val (textarea vs input), cssSelector (including id case, class case, nth-child), siblingElements, nextElementSibling, previousElementSibling, firstElementSibling, lastElementSibling, elementSiblingIndex, insertChildren (index positive and negative), prepend/append string HTML. We need to test that shadowChildrenRef cache is invalidated after modifications. Also test that nodelistChanged leads to null shadow reference. We can use simple HTML parsing to create a Document and get elements. We'll import org.jsoup.Jsoup, Document, etc. Write @Before method to set up a base Element tree. Test cases: 1. testTagNameAndTag: create new Element("div") and assert tagName = "div", tag() not null, isBlock true for div. 2. testTagNameChange: element.tagName("span") changes tag, assert. 3. testAttributes: attr set and get, boolean attr. 4. testDataset: set data-attribute via attr, dataset returns map. 5. testParentAndParents: parse HTML "

After calling children() and storing reference? Since it's private, we can test that after appendElement new child, previous list does not contain new child? Not easily accessible. But we can test that after calling children(), then appendElement another child, subsequent children() includes new child (cache refreshed). The method resets shadowChildrenRef in nodelistChanged which is called by NodeList on changes. So after appending, children() should reflect new child. 8. testTextAndOwnText: element with mixed content:

Use DataNode perhaps. 11. testClassMethods: element with class attribute; test className, classNames set, addClass, removeClass, toggleClass, hasClass. 12. testCssSelector: element with id returns "#id".
